title: Microsoft Purview Endpoint DLP: expanded controls for local AI agents
summary: Hold: a policy sync status other than Updated does not mean a device receives no policies or has no protection. Microsoft documents that older policies can remain enforced and that Not available can reflect missing status information; the roadmap facts and the existing control routes otherwise check out.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe the local-agent Endpoint DLP extension or a feature-specific control to configure today.

Results describe existing endpoint controls or separate Agent 365/cloud-agent protections, not this extension.

claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint local agents DLP default licensing price meter' and 'Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported agent interaction points Windows macOS configuration default account evaluation'; read roadmap and endpoint-dlp-learn-about. No default for this extension was stated.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the list of agents supported by these new Endpoint DLP controls.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported agent interaction points Windows macOS configuration default account evaluation'; read endpoint-dlp-learn-about and Defender discovery search excerpts. Defender's discovery support matrix does not establish support for this DLP extension.

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Open questions
claims.claim: Microsoft has not published the supported interaction points for the new controls.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported agent interaction points Windows macOS configuration default account evaluation'; read endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-configure-endpoint-settings. Neither enumerates this extension's interaction points.

claims.claim: The operating systems supported by the local-agent controls are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported agent interaction points Windows macOS configuration default account evaluation'; opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about. Its general Endpoint DLP OS matrix does not identify support for these local-agent controls.

claims.claim: Local AI agents run on users' devices.
claims.quote: Defender discovers local AI agents on Windows and macOS endpoints. This includes agents that run from the command line, desktop apps, agentic IDEs, VS Code extensions, and Claw-based local agent implementations.
claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/defender-endpoint/local-agent-discovery-overview to sources for the statement that local agents run on endpoint devices; do not imply its discovery coverage establishes DLP coverage.

claims.where: What's changing; Scope: Users and devices
claims.claim: Endpoint DLP generally covers Windows 10/11, macOS and certain Windows server versions.
claims.quote: Endpoint data loss prevention (Endpoint DLP) extends the activity monitoring and protection capabilities of DLP to Windows 10/11, macOS (the three latest released major versions) devices, and Windows certain server versions.

claims.where: Scope; Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Devices must be onboarded to be used as locations for Endpoint DLP policies.
claims.quote: You need to onboard all the devices you want to use as locations in your DLP policies.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure, second bullet
claims.claim: Devices whose policy sync status is not Updated would not receive policies.
claims.quote: However, the outdated policy that exists on the offline device will still be enforced.
claims.fix: Replace the bullet with: 'Devices must be onboarded to use Endpoint DLP. A policy sync status of Updated confirms receipt of the latest policy version; other statuses require investigation and do not by themselves establish that no policy is enforced.' The sync reference also says Not available can mean device properties are unavailable: https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-edlp-tshoot-sync.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not stated which account or component evaluates the new agent interactions.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported agent interaction points Windows macOS configuration default account evaluation'; opened endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-configure-endpoint-settings. No identity or evaluation component specific to this extension was documented.

claims.claim: The experience of a block for a person or local agent is not documented for this extension.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP agent interaction block override identity operating systems'; read endpoint-dlp-learn-about and existing block-action search results. Existing user notifications and cloud Agent 365 behaviour do not describe this local-agent extension.

claims.claim: Override availability for these local-agent actions is not yet documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP agent interaction block override identity operating systems'; read endpoint-dlp-learn-about and dlp-create-deploy-policy. General Block with override documentation does not specify override support for this extension.

claims.claim: Existing Microsoft DLP guidance recommends incremental deployment through simulation and a pilot group before full enforcement.
claims.quote: Always take an incremental approach to deploying a policy, starting from the least impactful DLP simulation mode through full enforcement.

claims.claim: The simulation and pilot deployment experience for the new agent controls is not specifically documented.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP local AI agents settings PowerShell supported'; opened dlp-create-deploy-policy, endpoint-dlp-create-policy-device-scoping and endpoint-dlp-learn-about. No deployment experience specific to this extension was described.

claims.claim: The policy creation and deployment page requires membership in Compliance administrator, Compliance data administrator, Information Protection, Information Protection Admin or Security administrator.
claims.quote: The account you use to create and deploy policies must be a member of one of these role groups: Compliance administrator; Compliance data administrator; Information Protection; Information Protection Admin; Security administrator

claims.claim: Roles specific to configuring the new local-agent controls are not yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP local AI agents settings PowerShell supported' and 'Purview Endpoint DLP local AI agents supported agent interaction points Windows macOS configuration default account evaluation'; read dlp-create-deploy-policy. Only existing policy roles were described.

claims.claim: The Devices policy route is Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies > Create policy > Enterprise applications & devices > Custom > Custom policy > Devices.
claims.quote: Select Create policy. Select Enterprise applications & devices. Select the Custom from the Categories then Custom policy template from Regulations. ... Scope the location to only the Devices location.

claims.claim: New-DlpCompliancePolicy -Name <String> -EndpointDlpLocation <MultiValuedProperty> creates a policy with Endpoint DLP user scope.
claims.quote: The EndpointDLPLocation parameter specifies the user accounts to include in the DLP policy for Endpoint DLP when they are logged on to an onboarded device. You identify the account by name or email address. You can use the value All to include all user accounts.

claims.claim: Per-device policy sync status is reached through Microsoft Purview portal > Settings > Device onboarding > Devices.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Settings (gear icon in the upper right corner) > Device onboarding > Devices. ... Select a device to open the details pane for more information on the policy sync status.
claims.fix: Extend controls[1].ui.path and the repeated guidance path to 'Settings > Device onboarding > Devices > device'. The source continues by selecting a device to open its policy sync status details.

claims.claim: DeviceInfo | where DlpInfo != "" is a read-only Advanced hunting query in the Microsoft Defender portal that returns Endpoint DLP device data, including policy sync information.
claims.quote:
DeviceInfo 
| where DlpInfo != ""
| project DlpInfo

The JSON object can be used to query and report on device configuration status, policy synchronization status, Endpoint DLP enablement, and other configuration details for onboarded devices.

claims.where: controls[2].ui and api; controls[0].note; Governance controls
claims.claim: No UI setting or automation specific to selecting local AI agents and interaction points is documented, and existing Devices policy creation is not documented as the configuration route for this extension.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Endpoint DLP local AI agents settings PowerShell supported'; read endpoint-dlp-learn-about, dlp-configure-endpoint-settings, device-scoping instructions and New-DlpCompliancePolicy; search returned Set-PolicyConfig and Set-DlpComplianceRule, not a local-agent interaction selector.

claims.where: Governance controls; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Policy sync status reports whether a device received the latest policy version; monitoring that status does not change policy coverage.
claims.quote: The Policy sync status shows you if the device received the latest policy version, or if the corresponding policies synced successfully to the device.
